title: One Burning Question for Every Premier League Club After 10 Games
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:00 PM ESTWe’re in the thick of it now. / Eston Parker/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesTen games into the 2026–27 Premier League season, and we are starting to get a feel for this campaign.
We are now, very much, in the thick of it. We’ve seen title ambitions fall away, surprise packages emerge, summer signings excel and flop.
At this stage, there’s a lot we already know. But there are still a lot of unknowns on the table.
As domestic soccer returns from the November international break, here are some of the burning questions that need answering.

Look who’s back. /  David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesHaving lots of quality players to pick from is the archetypal “nice headache” for a manager to have. Even nicer when you’re sitting pretty at the top of the league.
Still, Mikel Arteta’s first-world problem of having to choose between the in-form Ezri Konsa and returning William Saliba threatens to become more than a head-scratcher.
The Gunners have key games on the horizon against Manchester City, Brentford, Spurs and Manchester United and will be wary of changing a winning formula. Can Arteta keep everyone happy and on song?
Konsa wins duels, Saliba allows them to play a higher line. Decisions, decisions...

We’ve seen our fair share of exasperated Emery this season. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesVilla’s six-match unbeaten Premier League run is all well and good, but they really should have finished off both Fulham and United.
Unai Emery’s men are too often getting caught up in frantic, end-to-end games and need to find a way to slow it down and take control of the ride.
Villa rank 15th in the Premier League for average possession this season, but third for the most times dispossessed.

Just like watching Madrid. / Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesIn Europe’s big five leagues, only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid and Bournemouth have won their last eight games. It’s just the latest mind-boggling stat for anyone who still remembers the Cherries as EFL bottom feeders.
Marco Rose’s men are Opta’s favorites to go all the way in the Europa League this season and have, so far, not let European commitments distract them on the domestic front.

Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier and Rayan currently look like one of the continent’s most potent front threes, while Eli Junior Kroupi is ready to come back into the mix as we head into the busy period of what could be an historic season for the club.

Igor Thiago’s difficult second album. / MB Media/Getty ImagesThe Bees’ big Brazilian was one of the breakout stars of 2025–26, as he bagged 22 Premier League goals. It was the most ever by a Brazilian in England’s top flight.
While Thiago has hardly flopped this season, he clearly isn’t hitting the same heights, with just two league goals in ten games in 2026–27.
A disappointing summer World Cup with Brazil may have taken a toll on the striker, while opposition defenders appear to be paying special attention to his movements.

Brentford are sharing the goals out nicely this season, but could use a little more from their spearhead. The 25-year-old has significantly underperformed his xG (4.5) and ranks among the Premier League’s highest for touches in the opposition box, suggesting his dry spell could be temporary.

Are Brighton challengers? / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesAt what point do we seriously start considering Brighton as title challengers? Fabian Hürzeler’s men are the only team to beat Arsenal this season (and do so in some style), are the Premier League’s top scorers and are winning games with style, verve and real confidence.
